question.text: Sodium Carbonate cannot be used in place of $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$ for the identification of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, \mathrm{Ba}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Sr}^{2+}$ ions (in group $\mathrm{V}$ ) during mixture analysis because :

options.text: Concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_3{ }^{2-}$ ions is very low.
Sodium ions will react with acid radicals.
$\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions will interfere with the detection of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, \mathrm{Ba}^{2+}, \mathrm{Sr}^{2+}$ ions.

solution.text: If $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$ is used in place of $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$. It will precipitate group $\mathrm{V}$ radicals as well as magnesium radicals. The reason for this is the high ionization of $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$ in water into $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and $\mathrm{CO}_3^{--}$. Now the higher concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_3^{--}$is available which exceeds the solubility product of group $\mathrm{V}$ radicals as well as that of magnesium radicals.
